key_insight: A local, open-weight OCR+LLM pipeline on a consumer GPU can accurately extract structured clinical information from faxed referral packets without sending PHI to a commercial cloud model.
clinical_relevance: This could reduce manual chart review and help clinics organize incoming oncology referral information faster while keeping patient data on-device.
method: Generated 200 synthetic colorectal cancer referral packets from simulated records
Rendered packets as fax images with no text layer
Used local OCR (OvisOCR2) plus open-weight LLM extraction (Qwen3.8-27B) on consumer hardware
evidence_signal: On 140 validation packets, the system achieved 0.990 weighted accuracy, with exact extraction of lab values at 98.9%, dates at 99.7%, diagnoses at 100%, and no fabricated facts among 11,993 extracted facts.
watch_item: Results were based on synthetic referral packets, so real-world fax quality, document variation, and deployment workflows still need external validation.
paper_title: Extraction of clinical information from faxed medical records using a small local large language model pipeline on consumer hardware
